run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend since 2026-11-15T03:28:12Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The frontend RequestErrorRate alert is explained by an 8-minute gap in the ad service's availability caused by the ad Deployment rollout at 03:27:01–03:27:04. The only ad replica (ad-554b849958-gcmfq, ReplicaSet ad-554b849958) was deleted and replaced by a new pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz (new ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5, generation 2 / revision 2). The ad container has no readiness, liveness or startup probe, so the pod was marked Ready one second after the container started (03:27:03 → Ready 03:27:04) and became the single endpoint of the ad Service while its gRPC server was still booting: the container logged "Ad service starting." only at 03:31:14 and the ad service's own oteldemo.AdService/GetAds span counter stayed flat at 1312 from 03:28:00 to 03:35:30. During exactly that gap, the frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds error spans, GET /api/data error spans and GET (server) error spans all rose in lock-step (from 383/383/396 to 801/801/814), and frontend-proxy's ingress and router-frontend-egress error spans rose with them. Frontend error accumulation stopped after the 03:35 bucket, matching ad's GetAds counter resuming at 03:36:00. No other service's ERROR-status series increased in the window, and the frontend pod itself did not restart or redeploy. Root cause supported by evidence: the rollout replaced the only ad replica with a not-yet-listening instance that was advertised as Ready because no probe gates its endpoints.

claims.text: For service frontend, the cumulative STATUS_CODE_ERROR span counters for span_name="GET /api/data" and span_name="grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds" both went from 383 at 03:27:00 to 801 by 03:35:00, and span_name="GET" went from 396 to 814 over the same period; the increases begin in the 03:28:00 bucket and stop after 03:35:00. All other frontend operations' error counters (POST, GET /api/cart, POST /api/cart, POST /api/checkout, executing api route /api/cart, /api/checkout, grpc CartService/AddItem, CartService/GetCart, CheckoutService/PlaceOrder) stayed flat over 03:20–03:50.
Between 03:20:00 and 03:40:00 the frontend gained about 428.7 error spans versus about 668.7 non-error spans on span_name="GET /api/data" (roughly 39% of that route's spans errored in the window).

frontend-proxy carries the user-facing symptoms: between 03:20:00 and 03:40:00 span_name="ingress" gained about 450.3 STATUS_CODE_ERROR spans against about 13401 non-error spans, and span_name="router frontend egress" error spans rose from 456 at 03:20 to 874 by 03:40 and then stayed flat.

The ad Deployment "ad" is at generation 2, revision 2, single replica, strategy RollingUpdate (maxSurge 25%, maxUnavailable 25%) with minReadySeconds unset. Events show ReplicaSet ad-d89765fb5 SuccessfulCreate for pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz at 03:27:01 (Scheduled, Pulled, Created, Started container ad by 03:27:03) and, at 03:27:04, Pod ad-554b849958-gcmfq Killing and ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 SuccessfulDelete. ReplicaSet ad-554b849958 (created 02:54:34) now has 0 replicas and ad-d89765fb5 (created 03:27:01) has 1 ready.

Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz has readinessProbe, livenessProbe and startupProbe all null; its ad container started at 03:27:03 with restartCount 0, and the pod's Ready condition became True at 03:27:04, one second after container start.

The ad Service (selector opentelemetry.io/name=ad, port 8080 → targetPort 8080, matching the pod template labels app.kubernetes.io/name=ad, opentelemetry.io/name=ad) has exactly one endpoint, IP 100.96.1.122, which targetRef identifies as Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz.

The ad service's own span counter for span_name="oteldemo.AdService/GetAds", status_code STATUS_CODE_UNSET, was 1283 at 03:27:00, 1312 at 03:28:00, then flat at 1312 at every 30s step through 03:35:30, resuming at 1363 at 03:36:00 and 1422 at 03:37:00 — i.e. the ad service recorded no GetAds spans for roughly 7.5 minutes.

The only stdout line available from ad container ad-d89765fb5-whfnz in the window is "Ad service starting." at 2026-11-15T03:31:14.903167388Z, about 4 minutes after the container start time 03:27:03 recorded in the pod status.

The ad service's own spans carry no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series in 02:55–03:50; its only ERROR-status series are span_name="flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/EventStream" (1→2) and span_name="flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean", which is flat at 76 from 03:05 through 03:35 and then 148 from 03:37 onward.

Across all services in 03:20:00–03:50:00, the ERROR-status span series whose values increased are only frontend operations (GET, GET /api/data, executing api route (pages) /api/data, grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds, tcp.connect) and frontend-proxy operations (ingress, router frontend egress); the other returned ERROR series (accounting orders receive 1, ad EventStream/ResolveBoolean, fraud-detection EventStream/ResolveInt, payment GET/dns.lookup/tcp.connect, recommendation /flagd.../EventStream) stayed flat or changed only as noted for ad.

The frontend Deployment's ReplicaSet frontend-675fd7b5c5 was created 02:54:34 and is unchanged (1/1 ready), and pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 is Running with restartCount 0 and start time 02:54:34, so the frontend was not redeployed or restarted during the window.

The newest frontend traces Jaeger returned for the whole window start at 03:24:46 (5 traces, 78 spans); in that sample all frontend GET /api/products/{productId}, GET /api/recommendations and grpc client spans to ProductCatalogService and RecommendationService carry http.status_code=200 / rpc.grpc.status_code=0, and there are no error-tagged spans.

The RequestErrorRate alert on frontend is caused by the ad Deployment rollout at 03:27:01–03:27:04: the single ad replica was replaced by ad-d89765fb5-whfnz, which was advertised as the ad Service endpoint immediately (no readiness/startup probe) while its gRPC listener on port 8080 was not yet accepting traffic; frontend's grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls failed from the 03:28 bucket until about 03:35, which returned errors on the /api/data route and produced the frontend request error rate (and the matching frontend-proxy ingress 5xx).

Residual/secondary candidate: the ad service's flagd client calls show ERROR status (flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean rising from 76 to 148 between 03:35 and 03:37, EventStream 1→2). If flag evaluation in the new ad pod were failing, ad could return degraded/error responses; the evidence does not tie this to the frontend error burst, because the same ResolveBoolean ERROR counter was already flat at 76 while ad served normally before 03:27 and it only moved after ad resumed processing spans, so its effect on GetAds responses remains unproven.

Rejected: the frontend itself being restarted or redeployed explains the error burst. frontend-675fd7b5c5 has existed since 02:54:34, pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-c8fk6 has restartCount 0, and no frontend ReplicaSet/pod create-or-delete events were returned for the window; the errors therefore originate in a dependency call, not in a frontend rollout.

Rejected as the trigger: a pod crash, OOM or eviction of ad. Pod ad-d89765fb5-whfnz is Running with restartCount 0 and no previous container instance, and the events for the ad objects are only Scheduled/Pulled/Created/Started plus ReplicaSet SuccessfulCreate and the old pod's Killing/SuccessfulDelete — the old pod was replaced by its controller as a rollout, and no Evicted or OOMKilled evidence exists for the ad workload.

Frontend error spans show the /api/data route is not wholly broken: in 03:20:00–03:40:00 it still recorded about 668.7 non-error versus about 428.7 error spans, and the frontend GET /api/products/{productId} and GET /api/recommendations paths recorded no error increase at all — the failure is confined to the ad-dependent path, not to the whole frontend.

Add a readinessProbe (gRPC or TCP on port 8080) and/or a startupProbe to the ad container so the pod only enters the ad Service endpoints once its listener accepts connections, and consider minReadySeconds plus 2 replicas with maxUnavailable 0 so a single-replica rolling update cannot leave the service with zero serving endpoints while the JVM boots.

gaps: What triggered the ad Deployment update to generation 2 / revision 2 at 03:27 is unknown: the change_history integration is not available. Both the old ReplicaSet and the new one reference image tag ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-ad, and the deleted pod's image digest could not be read to compare with the new pod's imageID ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo@sha256:c9d4f94314937eb3b61cf8b1672b7e87fab95442bd1d01f8d32f43a882255944.

The exact Alertmanager rule expression for RequestErrorRate and the units of its reported value 2.355555555555555 could not be read: list_prometheus_rules filtered by rule_name=RequestErrorRate returned no data, so how the error rate is computed and against which denominator is unknown.

Per-span failure detail for the failing GetAds calls is unknown: traces_search for frontend in 03:28–03:40 returned no traces (no data), the newest frontend traces in Jaeger are at 03:24:46, and traces_search for ad in 03:40–03:50 returned no traces, so the gRPC status of the failing calls (e.g. UNAVAILABLE vs connection refused) cannot be confirmed from spans.

Application-level error text is unverified: the frontend container returned zero log lines, the ad container has only the single "Ad service starting." line, and there is no previous ad container instance to read; the ad filtered log query for error keywords returned no data.

rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_count and any rpc_*/http_server_*/app_* metric names returned no series for the queried selector, so gRPC status-code breakdowns and server-side latency/error codes for the failing frontend→ad calls are unknown.

No ERROR-status series was returned at all for cart, checkout, currency, email, image-provider, product-catalog, quote, shipping, kafka and load-generator in 03:20–03:50, and no ERROR series was returned for service_name=flagd; for those entities the error status is unknown, not zero, so they can be neither listed as affected nor certified healthy from these queries.

End-customer/downstream impact beyond the frontend-proxy ingress error spans (for example load-generator failures or abandoned checkouts) is unverified; load-generator has no ERROR-status series returned.

The significance of ad's flagd.evaluation.v1.Service/ResolveBoolean ERROR spans (76 → 148) cannot be determined: no traces or logs cover the new pod's startup window, and no flagd-side error series was returned.
next_steps: Review the deployment/CI record that produced ad Deployment generation 2 at 03:27:01 to identify the intended pod-template change (change history integration is not available to this investigation).

Add a readinessProbe or startupProbe on ad port 8080 (and minReadySeconds) so future rollouts do not route traffic to a booting JVM; if a near-term fix is needed, run two ad replicas with maxUnavailable 0.

Capture the gRPC status codes of the failing grpc.oteldemo.AdService/GetAds calls (OTel span attributes or rpc_client_duration_milliseconds_* series) to confirm the connection-level failure mode before closing the incident.

Verify whether alert RequestErrorRate's threshold and units (reported value 2.355555555555555) match the observed ~39% error share on GET /api/data and the frontend-proxy ingress error ratio, and confirm the alert has cleared since frontend error counters stopped growing after 03:35.

query.jq_expr: .items[] | select(.metadata.name | test("^ad$|^frontend$")) | {name: .metadata.name, selector: .spec.selector, ports: .spec.ports, clusterIP: .spec.clusterIP}

view.cannot_prove: Objects are the cluster's state when the query ran, not during the incident window: they cannot prove what was true earlier, and an object missing now may have existed then. Events cover only their own timestamps inside the window; an event that is not returned is unknown, not proof nothing happened (events expire and timestamps are often null). A jq result is what the expression selected, not a full picture of the kind.
